title: Texas City refinery: measure the hazard you intend to control
focus: Steady production and favorable injury statistics do not establish readiness for a hazardous startup.

sources.title: CSB BP Texas City Final Investigation Report
sources.locator: Executive summary; section 1.6 findings; sections 9.3–9.4 on management and indicators
sources.limitations: Relevant sections inspected; this is not a reconstruction of every event or finding.

facts.statement: The accident occurred during startup of the isomerization unit; a flooded distillation tower and atmospheric release exposed people near occupied trailers.
The CSB found that reliance on low personal-injury rates gave a misleading picture of process-safety performance.

retrospective.boundary: Process equipment, startup state, instrumentation, staffing, temporary occupied buildings, maintenance, and management measures belong to the hazard boundary.
interfaces: Operating mode → protection: startup changes inventories and actions relative to normal production.
Management metric → resource decision: a convenient metric may omit the accident mechanism of concern.

decision.question: Which evidence should support a startup readiness claim?
options: Use recent production availability and personal-injury performance.
Check mode-specific protection, instrumentation, procedures, staffing, and occupied-area exposure.
decision.recommendation: Build measures around barriers to the major hazard and their observed condition.
decision.uncertainty: A barrier checklist still needs demonstrated functionality and authority to act on deficiencies.

rows: Confirm mode-specific limits and instrument validity
Independent checks of inventory and protective functions
Review temporary occupancy against credible releases
Track unresolved barrier impairments with consequence
Age, ownership, and verified closure of impairments

questions: Why can a declining injury rate coexist with increasing major-accident risk?
What changes when a plant enters a transient operating mode?
Write a management brief that distinguishes output performance from protection health.
answer_signals: Links each measure to a mechanism and a decision.
Includes temporary facilities and contractors in the system boundary.
Avoids substituting completed paperwork for demonstrated protection.
retrospective.transfer_exercise: Synthetic: a plant dashboard is green while three protective functions are bypassed. Redesign the decision-relevant portion of the dashboard.
retrospective.limits: The artifact is not a refinery operating procedure and does not establish safe staffing, siting distances, or protection settings.
